headline: "One chemical composition, one CR": geo-tagged, government-issued proof of every import source; no 9(4) TI source endorsement where the composition differs; Indoxacarb composition committee formed; botanicals get the same shelf-life rules as chemicals.

changes.d: On HPMA's 'Make in India' representation, all registered import sources must give manufacturing and office addresses with geo-tagging, backed by government-issued documents of the source country (e.g. manufacturing licence). New applicants must submit this with the application; it becomes part of the guidelines.

A 9(4) TI endorsement of an additional source is not allowed if its chemical composition differs from the granted CR; a fresh 9(4) TI CR is needed. Validity extension, address or purity endorsements are refused for sources whose composition does not match the 9(3) registrant.
A committee was set up to correct the chemical composition of Indoxacarb products (isomer issue). Its rule came in the 477th meeting.
Atul's Indoxacarb + Emamectin EC was rejected: end-use products that cause irreversible eye damage (Category 1) are not registered (398th RC rule).

changes.t: Botanicals: shelf-life rules as for chemicals
changes.d: Neem/Azadirachtin and other botanical products follow the same shelf-life extension guidelines as chemical pesticides.

changes.t: Paraquat TI from a new source approved
changes.d: Tropical Agrosystem's Paraquat dichloride technical 45% was approved from a new source (before the later ban).
FMC's dossier was generated with 96–99% material while 97% is sought; purity must follow the in-house rule based on US EPA registration.
Nasham Crop Care objected to the affidavit-on-NJSP and partner NOC conditions; the endorsement letter is issued without insisting on them until the applicant is heard.

actions: Importers: collect geo-tagged, government-issued address proof of each source.
9(4) TI: check that the new source's composition matches before seeking an endorsement.
